chunks: Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Whenever you see the crescent moon, fast; and when you see it (again), break the fast. And it is not by opinion, nor by guessing. And the sighting is not that ten persons stand, one of them says 'It is there', while nine look but cannot see it. Rather, if one sees it, a thousand (can) see it.

key_terms.التظني: Guessing/speculation — explicitly rejected alongside personal opinion
key_terms.الرأي: Opinion/personal judgment — explicitly rejected as a basis for moon sighting
key_terms.الرؤية: The sighting/observation — the valid legal criterion for establishing the lunar month
key_terms.الهلال: The crescent/new moon — the determining marker for the Islamic lunar calendar months

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on moon sighting for Ramadan according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes the jurisprudential principle for beginning and ending Ramadan: visual sighting of the crescent moon (ru'yah) is required, and must be verifiable — that is, visible to many people simultaneously under clear conditions. The ruling rejects subjective opinion or guesswork as a basis for determining the start or end of the fasting month. The principle 'if one sees it, a thousand see it' sets a standard of widespread confirmability for a valid moon sighting.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Whenever you see the new moon, so (begin) Fasting, and when you see it (again) so break the Fasting, and it is not by opinions, nor by the guessing, and the sighting is not that ten persons are standing so one of them is saying, ‘It is that’, and ten are waiting but cannot see it. Rather, if one can see, so a thousand can see it (too)’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ahmad has narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

When you see the crescent, then fast and when you see the crescent (again), then discontinue fasting. It is not by opinions and conjectures. If out of ten people only one says that there is the crescent but the rest cannot see, it is not seeing. If one can see a thousand can also see.’”
